title: SDK mini-workshop playset + content backlog
body:
Goal: a repeatable 30–45 minute mini-workshop that gets engineers from zero -> instrumented SDK call with basic telemetry and a smoke test. This doc is a playset (agenda + assets list + quick snippets) + a content backlog for short-form collateral. Status: working draft; intended for hands-on sessions run by DE reps and for inclusion in self-serve labs later.

1) Core constraints / design principles
- Keep idempotent: all exercises should be runnable in <30 minutes on laptop with free account keys.
- Minimal deps: Node (latest LTS) and Python examples only; no Docker required.
- Observable by default: instrument 5 telemetry events + one latency histogram.
- Failure-safe: provide sample network/cold-start mitigation guidance.

2) 30m running agenda (fast path)
- 0–3m: intro + expected outputs (demo of chat/embeds)
- 3–8m: set up CLI creds + scaffold (git clone, npm/pip install)
- 8–18m: Make first call (hello world generation) + streaming quickcheck
- 18–26m: Add telemetry hook (event names below) and run smoke assertion (tokens < threshold, status 200)
- 26–30m: Failover toggle demo: swap to local stub to show graceful degradation
- Stretch: 30–45m: add one prompt evaluation test and compare outputs across two model presets

3) Assets to ship (MVP):
- repo: workshop-stub (template code + README + smoke tests)
- one-pager: "30m SDK micro-workshop" (slides + speaker notes)
- short gifs: creds setup, streaming response, telemetry dashboard snapshot
- lab checklist: pre-reqs, firewall notes, known flaky networks

4) Code snippets (kept tiny for doc)
- Node quickstart (pseudo):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize X in 20 words' }] });
  console.log(res.text);

- Python quickstart (pseudo):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
  out = c.generate('Explain mutexes simply')
  print(out.text)

5) Telemetry & smoke assertions (consistent names)
- events: ["sdk.start", "sdk.request.sent", "sdk.token.received", "sdk.request.error", "sdk.test.assertion"]
- tags: model, region, sample_app, cadence
- minimal histogram: request.latency_ms (buckets at 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000)
- smoke assertions: HTTP 200, tokens_consumed < 300 (configurable), response not empty, latency < 1000ms for demo model

6) Failure modes & recovery steps (teaching moments)
- 401/invalid key: repro steps + quick copy of how to rotate key in console
- High latency: toggle to 'fast-latency' model variant and re-run smoke
- Partial streams: instruct to fall back to non-streaming call and capture full output
- Networking (company VPNs): add note to disable corporate proxy for labs or use personal hotspot

7) Content backlog (prioritized)
- 1: workshop repo + one-pager guide + speaker notes (MVP)
- 2: 3x short gifs for marketing/devexp pages
- 3: quick video (5m) demonstrating failover + telemetry dashboard walkthrough
- 4: multi-language snippet pack (Go + Java + Ruby) – stretch goal
- 5: canonical smoke test suite to run in CI for SDKs

8) Measurement & success criteria
- adoption metrics: workshops run, repos forked, CI runs of smoke tests
- qualitative: participant self-report (post-lab survey: 3 questions)
- technical: % of sessions where students complete full fast path in <30m

9) Operational checklist for running a session
- pre-run: verify workshop repo token seeded, slide deck open, telemetry dashboard template ready
- during-run: record participant issues (channel + short GitHub issue template)
- post-run: collect feedback, convert top 3 pain points into tickets, schedule follow-up docs work

10) Open questions / TODOs
- Can we include an offline stub that simulates prefix caching behavior? (Priya to prototype)
- What's the minimal user-space telemetry SDK we can ship to avoid DIY instrumentation? (SRE consult)
- Decide canonical demo model set (cost vs latency tradeoffs) – propose: redwood-1-small (demo), redwood-1-medium (compare)

Notes for follow-ups: create small GH issues for each backlog item, run two internal pilot workshops (DE + Solutions Eng) and capture timestamps for friction points. Keep this doc lean — intended to be copy/pasted into a more formal Confluence page once MVP assets exist."
